feature: Ask says what it is doing while it works
summary: While Ask works on a request, its row in the Agent panel now carries one live line under the request saying what it is doing right now (getting the model ready, reading your request with how far through, writing the steps, planning, painting with how far through, turning it into layers, checking, trying again and why), with the time once a stage passes five seconds. The line goes when the request lands. An agent sees the same line in list_documents.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default, built-in model and picture model set up in Settings > Ask.

try.do: Open an empty picture and press Command K.
Type: a fox in a forest at sunset, then press Return.
Watch the Agent group on the right: under the request, the grey line says Getting the model ready, then Reading your request with a rising percent.
Keep watching as it moves to Writing the steps, Planning, and Painting with its percent.
Watch it say Turning it into layers, then Checking it.
Hover the line to read the whole of a line cut short.
When it lands, check the row says what it made and the live line is gone.
Play the reel 2026-11-01-ask-says-what-it-is-doing-reel.mp4 (the panel through a whole request, a frame every 2.5 s) or open the contact sheet 2026-11-01-ask-says-what-it-is-doing-sheet.png.

evaluate: Can you tell at a glance that it is moving and roughly how far along it is, at any moment of the request?
Is 'Reading your request, 41%' the right words for the minute the model spends taking in the request, or would you rather it said something else?
Is the grey line under the request quiet enough, or does it pull your eye while you work on the canvas?
Does the time on the right (10s, 1:05) help, or is the percent enough on its own?
rough: No mock covers a request at work: the Agent group mock (agent-generate-wt.html) shows only finished rows, so this goes further than the mock and removes nothing from it.

Stages and timings measured on real requests at Next defaults (walks ask-says-what-it-is-doing-walk and ask-says-what-it-is-doing-across-requests-walk): the fox, 144 s, longest without a new line 10.9 s (Getting the model ready, which shows its time); the cat playing a guitar scene, 122 s, longest 7.8 s; make the cat black (an edit to the picked drawing), 136 s, longest 10.2 s (the last stretch of reading the request, which shows its time). Reading moves about every 2.5 s and painting every 3 to 4.7 s.

The photo and the component sheet were not measured: the walk that runs them stopped itself when you came back to the Mac (it needs the probe in front). Both go through the same reading and writing lines; the photo also gets the painter's percent.

'Reading your request' is the model taking in everything sent with the request (about 15,000 tokens of instructions, tools and the document). Its percent is against Ask's own estimate of that size, because the model's server never says the whole; it is held under 100% and has finished between 87% and 92% so far.

An edit to a picked layer reads its whole request twice (once more after it looks at the layers), so its percent climbs to about 90%, starts again at about 76% and climbs again. That is honest but can look like going backwards. The 136 s it took for 'make the cat black' is the model reading a long request with a picture of the canvas in it, not this line.

When a drawing lands, its layer is picked and its sections pushed the Agent group out of view during the check and any try again (seen in frame 57 of the first reel). The group is now brought back into view once the drawing lands, the same way a finished request already does; that fix is built and tested but has not been filmed yet, because the re-run waits for the Mac to be free.
Long subjects are cut to fit the panel's 40 character line, keeping the part and percent ('Painting a fox in a forest at…, 44%'); the whole line is on the tooltip and in list_documents.
